==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
According to the ''Oxford English Dictionary'', early usage refers to lines that do not move, such as one used in angling. Slightly later American usage refers to a boundary in a prison which prisoners must not cross. There is only indirect evidence that the sense of "due date" may be connected with this use of the term in prison camps during the American Civil War, when it referred to a physical line or boundary beyond which prisoners were shot.<ref>{{cite-web |title=Andersonville Prison |url=http://www.civilwar.org/education/history/warfare-and-logistics/warfare/andersonville.html |accessdate=23 April 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307140856/http://www.civilwar.org/education/history/warfare-and-logistics/warfare/andersonville.html |archivedate=7 March 2017 }}</ref> In 1904, in a report from the [[w:United States Department of Commerce and Labor|US Department of Commerce and Labor]], the term is used for "minimum work goals" (and in contrast to ''bonus line''): for example, as a typographer the line could be 18,000 [[w:Em (typography)|ems]] per day; should one not cross this line, then that could have negative consequences.<ref>{{cite book |last=Wright |first=C. D. |year=1904 |title=Regulation and Restriction of Output |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |location=United States |pages=53–56 |pageurl=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Regulation_and_Restriction_of_Output/l_VMAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22dead%20line%22&pg=PA53&printsec=frontcover |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Regulation_and_Restriction_of_Output/l_VMAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22dead%20line%22&pg=PA53&printsec=frontcover}}</ref> In 1917, the term is attested as a printing term for a guideline on the bed of a printing press beyond which text will not print. Three years later, the term is found in print in the sense of "time limit" in the closely connected publishing industry, indicating the time after which material would not make it into a newspaper or periodical.<ref>{{cite-web |title=The Mavens' Word of the Day |url=http://www.randomhouse.com/wotd/index.pperl?date=20000420 |accessdate=16 October 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016215332/http://www.randomhouse.com/wotd/index.pperl?date=20000420 |archivedate=16 October 2013 }}</ref>

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈdɛdˌlaɪn/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-deadline.wav|a=UK}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛdlaɪn|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A time limit in the form of a [[date]] on or before which something must be [[complete]]d.
#: {{syn|en|closing date}}
#: {{ux|en|I must make this '''deadline''' or my boss will kill me!}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[guideline]] marked on a [[plate]] for a [[printing press]].
# {{lb|en|archaic}} A line that does not move. {{rfex|en}} <!--what kind of line?!-->
# {{lb|en|archaic}} A [[boundary]] around a [[prison]], prisoners crossing which would be shot.
